context: Request: the longest-running matter that is still open (excluding shelved matters, counting matters in closing wind-down as open) and its opening date. Rubric: 1044-00006 (Thalassa Shipping, charter-party breach defense), opened October 16, 2023, plus a precision criterion.

stages.stage: List files in the document store
stages.note: Whole-store glob plus a read of the store folder (rejected as a directory).

stages.stage: Read documents picked from the file listing
stages.note: Three batches of reads from the six matters at the top of the listing: engagement letters and an opening memo, then closing memos and emails, then filings and checklists; no search at all.

stages.stage: Read a chosen matter's documents in depth
stages.note: Reads later parts of two closing emails of the two matters it is weighing.
Writes one listing-top matter whose deal had closed as the oldest open matter, treating its post-closing work as wind-down.

runs.sequence: List files in the document store → Read documents picked from the file listing → Read a chosen matter's documents in depth → Write the response → Finish the run
runs.failure_point: Never searched; picked the oldest of the six matters visible in a capped listing and treated a closed deal as still open.

first_error.stage: Read documents picked from the file listing
first_error.why: Chose what to read from the six matters in a capped listing without any search for open-matter status or opening dates, so the matter it needed never surfaced.

other_errors.why: It counted a matter whose transaction had already closed as still open by reading the closing-posture allowance loosely, so even among the matters it saw it named one that does not meet the request.

stages.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
stages.note: Reads engagement letters, a post-closing letter and a strategy memo of the oldest matters in that partial output.
Writes the oldest matter from the scan output, whose financing had closed, as still open in post-closing posture.

divergence: All three runs failed the same way: the matter they needed never appeared in any tool result. T0 and T2 never searched and judged the whole store from the six matters at the top of a capped listing (partial listing as corpus, at the reading stage). T1 read the same six matters, then ran a scan whose output it cut to the first 240 lines, which stopped at the lowest-numbered matters (search miss, at the scan stage). All three then named an old matter whose deal had closed as still open, reading the closing-posture allowance loosely (later over-inclusion at the write stage).
